featured_reviews.name: Paritosh Shiledar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Passport Seva Kendra Malad– Detailed Experience Review

Appointment & Arrival
My reporting time was 9:15 AM and appointment time 9:30 AM. I reached the location around 8:30 AM, which helped a lot since there were only two people ahead of me.

---

Location & Accessibility

The centre is located in a busy market area with street vendors and vegetable sellers near the entrance, so the surroundings feel crowded. However, accessibility is good and the location is not far from the Western Express Highway.

---

Parking

Parking is available for passport applicants in the basement of an adjacent building. I was able to park my car easily, probably because I arrived early. Security guards near the parking area are helpful, though they do tend to ask for tips (I ended up giving ₹20 each). Capacity for parking is unclear, so early arrival is advisable.

---

Process & Timeline

The overall process is systematic but involves multiple steps:

1. Entry & Photocopy Counter
Since I arrived early, I was allowed inside earlier than my reporting time. The first step was a photocopy counter where I had to buy a ₹4 Tatkal undertaking form.

2. Token Counter
Documents and originals were checked, and a token was issued.

3. Counter A
Documents were scanned and uploaded, and the photograph was taken. Once uploaded, documents become accessible across Counters A, B, and C.
Staff here (likely privately recruited) were professional and polite.

4. Waiting Area → Counter B
After Counter A, applicants wait until their token appears on the screen. Counter B mainly verifies originals; in my case, very little interaction happened. The govt employee should have checked my originals. He just let me go to Counter C where queries were raised

5. Counter C (Final Approval)
This is the final approval stage handled by a gazetted officer.

---

Staff Experience

Counter A staff were professional and courteous.
Staff at Counters B and C (government employees) were noticeably less polite and less helpful. Interaction felt rigid and somewhat dismissive.

One important observation: despite alternative documents being listed on the passport website, acceptance seemed to depend heavily on officer discretion.

In my case:

I had a registered rent agreement as address proof.
The officer demanded a bank passbook as photo ID, which I had not carried.
My company photo ID (from a public listed company), although listed as acceptable online, was rejected.
Digilocker documents were also not accepted despite broader government policy supporting them and paperless bharat.

This makes the experience feel unpredictable and somewhat dependent on individual officers.

---

Overall Experience

The process was quick — I finished and exited by around 9:45 AM, which is impressive timing. However, I had to go back and forth between counters due to document preferences and verification issues.

**Pros**

* Fast processing when slots are less crowded
* Parking availability
* Organized digital workflow at Counter A

**Cons**

* Crowded surrounding area
* Informal expectation of tips near parking
* Inconsistent document acceptance
* Mixed professionalism across counters

All the best
